description: Lithium is a chemical element with symbol Li and atomic number 3. It is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal that under standard conditions is the least dense metal and the least dense solid element. Like all alkali metals, lithium is highly reactive and flammable, and must be stored in vacuum, inert atmosphere, or inert liquid.
uses: Lithium and its compounds have several industrial applications including heat-resistant glass and ceramics, lithium grease lubricants, flux additives for iron, steel and aluminium production, and lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries, which alone consume more than three-quarters of lithium production. Lithium-based drugs are useful as a mood stabilizer and antidepressant in the treatment of mental illness such as bipolar disorder. Lithium metal is often used in coolants for heat transfer applications due to its high specific heat capacity.
characteristics: Lithium is soft enough to be cut with a knife and has a silvery-white appearance that oxidizes to lithium oxide in air. It has the lowest density of all metals at 0.534 g/cm³ and can float on water and light hydrocarbon oils. Its melting point is 180.50°C and boiling point is 1,342°C, both the highest of all alkali metals, and it has a mass specific heat capacity of 3.58 kilojoules per kilogram-kelvin, the highest of all solids.
